test_title: PYST 18: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India lays down that ‘The allocation of seats in the Council of States to

be filled by representatives of the States and of the Union territories shall be in accordance with the provisions in that behalf contained in the fourth Schedule’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 80**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 80 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
 
• The Council of States is to be composed of representatives of the States and Union territories.
 
• The allocation of seats in the Council of States is specified in the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This article ensures that the representation of states and union territories in the Rajya Sabha is in accordance with the provisions laid out in the Fourth Schedule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 81**

 
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• It specifies the maximum number of seats in the Lok Sabha and the allocation of these seats among the States.
 
 
 
• **Article 82**
 
 
• Article 82 pertains to the readjustment of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies after each census.
 
• This article ensures periodic readjustments to reflect changes in the population.
 
 
 
• **Article 83**
 
 
• Article 83 specifies the duration of the Houses of Parliament.
 
• The Lok Sabha has a term of five years, unless dissolved sooner, while the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Schedule**
 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India allocates seats in the Rajya Sabha to each State and Union territory.
 
• This schedule ensures balanced representation of the States and Union territories in the Council of States.
